t: The mainland half of the old Kingdom of Sicily, ruled separately from Naples after the Sicilian Vespers of 1282.
Angevin, Aragonese, Spanish and Bourbon rulers made Naples one of Europe's largest cities and a centre of art and learning.
Its feudal baronage and heavy taxes fuelled revolts; in 1816 it merged with Sicily into the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
dyk: Though ruled from Naples, the kingdom officially kept the name Kingdom of Sicily while the island had kings of its own, which is why their union in 1816 was called the Two Sicilies.
